prerequisites: Prior courses such as Mechanics, Strength of Materials, Theory of Machines and Mechanisms are highly recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Calculate the maximum resistance of machine elements in static and dynamic stress states.
Design and calculate shafts and power shafts.
Select the most appropriate joining and support elements for shafts and axles.
Perform the calculation and design of power transmissions using flexible elements.
Perform the design and verification of gears for a power transmission using gears.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: Introduction to design. Safety in design.
Topic 2: Practical calculation of resistance. Static Resistance.
Topic 4: Rigid transmissions. Gears. Design, calculation and verification.
Henriot's simplified calculation method for cylindrical gears.
Simplified calculation method for conical gears.
General method for worm and worm wheel gears.
Topic 6: Shafts and axles. Bearings. Couplings.
Calculation of shafts under bending, torsion, and combined bending and torsion.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a total score equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 must be obtained from the sum of all components. A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required in the final theoretical-practical exam; otherwise, the final grade will be capped at 4.0. For extraordinary calls, the same evaluation criteria apply, retaining grades from laboratory and classroom practices, and requiring an exam with a minimum score of 4 out of 10. Differentiated evaluation consists of a single exam covering expository lectures and classroom practices for 90% of the grade, and laboratory practices content for the remaining 10%.
